note: INSYS Core domain model. Provenance p: S = stated in SRS, D = derived from an SRS requirement, P = proposed. tr = state transitions [from, to, trigger]. inv = [invariant, requirement IDs]. consumes = [event, reaction]. Relationships are [upstream, downstream, pattern, what flows].

contexts.name: Life Insurance
contexts.purpose: Owns life proposals, underwriting, policies, benefits, beneficiaries, premiums, cash values, loans, maturities, group life and life claims.

invariants.rule: Product version must be published, effective and available on the proposal's channel and date
Eligibility rules must pass before submission
Beneficiary nominations total 100%
Content is frozen after submission; only underwriting can change terms
Decision must be within the decider's authority matrix
All mandatory evidence received, or waived by someone with authority, before a final decision
Rule set version used is recorded so the decision can be reproduced

aggregates.name: LifePolicy

invariants.rule: References the approved product and rating versions it was issued under
Every alteration is checked against policy state, product rules and authority
Beneficiary shares total 100% at every effective date
Cash value and loans exist only for products that support them
Lapse and reinstatement follow the product's grace and reinstatement rules

aggregates.note: Design decision: SRS §21.2 lists LifeBenefit, LifeBeneficiary, LifePremiumSchedule and LifeCashValue as separate aggregates. We recommend making them entities inside LifePolicy, because rules such as "shares total 100%" and "alterations depend on policy state" span them and must hold in one transaction. §21.2 says boundaries are to be validated, so this needs confirming in ADR-003.

invariants.rule: Principal cannot exceed the product's maximum share of cash value
Policy must be in force when the loan is issued
Balance is the sum of its transactions and is never negative
Validates policy status, insured life, benefit eligibility, exclusions and claimant authority
Approval must be within the approver's authority
Decision records rationale, evidence, rules and authority
Only one open claim per benefit and event
Payee is validated before approval
Amount is calculated from the policy's product version

aggregates.name: GroupScheme

invariants.rule: A member's cover above the free cover limit needs underwriting evidence
Each member belongs to exactly one category

aggregates.note: Proposed. §21.2 defines no group life aggregate.

contexts.name: General Insurance
contexts.purpose: Owns quotes, proposals, risk objects, policies, coverages, endorsements, renewals, cancellations, claims, loss assessment and recoveries for motor, property, marine and commercial lines.

invariants.rule: An issued quote version is immutable; changes create a new version
Can only be accepted within its validity period
Premium always matches a recorded rating request

aggregates.name: GeneralProposal

invariants.rule: Based on exactly one accepted quote version

aggregates.note: Thin aggregate. Consider merging into GeneralQuote in ADR-003 if proposals carry no data beyond declarations.

invariants.rule: Attributes conform to the object type's schema version
Has a valuation basis whenever a value is set

aggregates.name: GeneralPolicy

invariants.rule: Can insure several risk objects
Coverages stay within product limits and sublimits
Policy premium equals the sum of its coverage premiums
Renewal, cancellation and reinstatement follow product rules

aggregates.note: GeneralCoverage, a separate aggregate in §21.2, is modelled as an entity here because coverage limits and premium totals must be consistent with the policy in one transaction.

invariants.rule: Effective date falls within the policy period
Premium change comes from a rating request
Changes are applied to the policy only after approval
Loss date is within the policy period and the cover is valid
Settlement applies excess, limits and valuation rules
Approval is within authority
Decision records rationale and evidence
Assessor is on an approved panel for the line
Recovered amounts are recorded as claim financial movements

consumes.reaction: Attach premium to quote or endorsement
Confirm cover where payment is a condition

contexts.name: Health Insurance
contexts.purpose: Owns schemes, memberships, dependants, benefit usage, eligibility, preauthorisation, medical claims, utilisation, provider payment runs and fraud cases.

invariants.rule: Every member category maps to a plan
Supports principal members, dependants and lifecycle changes
Dependants stay within type and age limits
One active plan option per member at any date
Waiting periods are fixed at enrolment

aggregates.name: BenefitAccumulator

invariants.rule: Used plus reserved never exceeds the limit
Updated only with optimistic locking, because many claims touch it

aggregates.note: Our model of SRS HealthBenefit usage. Benefit definitions themselves are static configuration. Kept small on purpose: it is the main concurrency hot spot.

invariants.rule: Immutable once recorded
Member is eligible on the service dates
Authorised amount does not exceed available benefit
Clinical review only by roles with clinical purpose
Expires automatically at the end of validity
Each line validates membership, cover, limits, tariff, preauthorisation and exclusions
Duplicates are detected before adjudication
Paid amount is at most allowed amount minus co-payment
Payments are traceable and reconcilable
Opened by a utilisation rule or by a person, never closed automatically
Includes only claims approved for payment before the cut-off
Run total equals the sum of its remittances
Indicators open a case; only an investigator concludes it

consumes.reaction: Reinstate suspended membership when contributions are paid

contexts.name: Product Factory
contexts.purpose: Owns product definitions and their governed versions: coverages, benefits, limits, exclusions, availability and document templates.

invariants.rule: Published versions are immutable
Any change to a published product creates a new version
Validated before publication: no missing parameters, invalid values or incompatible benefits
Approved test cases pass before publication
Publication needs maker-checker approval
Has an effective date
Product code is unique per tenant and never reused
Belongs to exactly one domain: Life, General or Health

consumes.reaction: Revalidate drafts that depend on changed static data

contexts.name: Rating
contexts.purpose: Calculates premiums from rating factors, tables and parameters, and keeps a reproducible record of every calculation.

invariants.rule: Immutable once calculated; a recalculation is a new record
Records the product, rating and rule versions used
Recalculating with the same inputs and versions gives the same result

consumes.reaction: Load new rating version into cache

contexts.name: Rules
contexts.purpose: Evaluates eligibility, underwriting, referral and decline rule sets and records each decision.

invariants.rule: Immutable; records rule set version, inputs and outcome

contexts.name: Party
contexts.purpose: Owns the identity of people and organisations, their contact details, identifiers, relationships, roles and consent.

invariants.rule: Kind (individual or organisation) never changes
A party can hold many roles
An identity number is unique per document type and country within a tenant
A merged party is read-only and points to its survivor
Personal data is used only for authorised purposes
Append-only; the latest record per purpose is the current consent

consumes.reaction: Flag a death claim on the insured party for review

contexts.name: Claims Framework
contexts.purpose: Provides what all domains share in claims: claim numbers, evidence, communications, fraud indicators, payment instructions and claim financial movements.

invariants.rule: One claim number per domain claim; a repeat registration returns the same number
Reserves, payments and recoveries are traceable financial movements
Append-only; a correction is a new movement
Outstanding reserve never goes below zero
Released only after maker-checker approval
Cannot exceed the domain's approved amount
Idempotent per claim and instruction

contexts.name: Workflow
contexts.purpose: Runs versioned business processes: tasks, queues, SLA timers, escalation, delegated authority and maker-checker approvals.

invariants.rule: Transitions follow the process definition version it started on
Each transition calls the owning domain's validation
Survives restarts and integration failures
Maker and checker are different people
Checker's authority covers the amount and type

contexts.name: Documents
contexts.purpose: Generates, stores, delivers, retains and disposes of documents, and audits access to sensitive ones.

invariants.rule: Stored in tenant-scoped storage with access control
Records the template and product versions it was generated from
Access to sensitive documents is audited
Not disposed of before its retention date or while on legal hold

contexts.name: Static Data
contexts.purpose: Maintains reference data, configuration and master data through governed change requests and versions.

aggregates.name: StaticDataChange

invariants.rule: Maker and checker differ for Tier 1
Tier 1 changes show impact and pass simulation before activation
Active periods for one code never overlap
Approved versions are immutable

tables: ref_ / cfg_ / mst_ tables in each owning schema

invariants.rule: Committed completely or not at all

contexts.name: Billing
contexts.purpose: Turns policy premiums into billing accounts, schedules, invoices, credit notes, arrears and refunds.

invariants.rule: Obligations come only from authorised policy and premium transactions
Arrears buckets follow configured ageing rules
References source policy, tenant, product, currency and dates
Never changed once issued; corrections are credit notes
Settled status reflects allocated payments
Approved before any payment is instructed

contexts.name: Payments
contexts.purpose: Initiates and tracks every inbound and outbound payment, allocates receipts, handles provider callbacks and reconciles against bank records.

invariants.rule: Idempotent: the same key never moves money twice
Every status change is recorded
An ambiguous outcome is Unknown and goes to reconciliation, never Succeeded
Final statuses never change except by an explicit reversal
Allocations never exceed the amount received
Released only after approval
Every unmatched or ambiguous item is investigated and resolved by a person

contexts.name: Financial Subledger
contexts.purpose: Turns business events into balanced, traceable journals, controls accounting periods, reconciles and exports to the insurer's general ledger.

invariants.rule: Debits equal credits
Traceable to its source business transaction
Never overwritten once posted
Corrections are reversal journals that reference the original
Records the posting rule version used
Posted only into an open accounting period
One journal per source event, enforced by the inbox
Only one open period per date per tenant
A closed period accepts no postings
Identifies unmatched, duplicated, delayed and inconsistent items

contexts.name: Distribution and Commission
contexts.purpose: Owns intermediaries, their appointments and product permissions, and calculates, adjusts, states and settles commission.

invariants.rule: Sells only products it holds a current permission for
A suspended intermediary cannot start new business
Records the plan version and source transaction
Effective-dated plan applies at the transaction date
A clawback always references the original entitlement
Approved before payment

contexts.name: Reinsurance
contexts.purpose: Calculates cessions under treaties and facultative arrangements, bills recoveries, and produces bordereaux and statements.
contexts.note: §21 defines no reinsurance entities, so all aggregates here are proposed.

invariants.rule: Reproducible from the arrangement and configuration versions
Linked to the underlying policy or risk
Traceable and reconcilable
One bordereau per treaty and period

contexts.name: Compliance and Reporting
contexts.purpose: Prepares, approves and submits regulatory returns, and runs operational reports under tenant-aware access rules.

invariants.rule: Approved by a compliance officer before submission

contexts.name: Analytics
contexts.purpose: Builds read-only projections for portfolio, underwriting, claims, financial and operational analysis.
contexts.note: No aggregates. Projections (for example fact_written_premium and fact_claims_incurred) are rebuilt from events.

consumes.event: All published domain and financial events

contexts.name: Integration
contexts.purpose: Exposes the API gateway, translates partner formats through adapters, delivers webhooks, and handles retries, dead letters and idempotency.

invariants.rule: Replayed only by an authorised operator
Retried with back-off up to the policy limit

contexts.name: Portals and Channels
contexts.purpose: Insurer, broker, customer and provider portals and partner channels.
contexts.note: No aggregates. Channels call module APIs through the gateway; authorisation is enforced in backend services (IAM-007).

contexts.name: Tenancy
contexts.purpose: Owns tenants, their isolation profile, entitlements, limits and lifecycle.

invariants.rule: Tenant identifier is unique and immutable
Onboarding, suspension, reactivation and termination follow workflows
Changing isolation profile requires an approved data migration

contexts.name: Identity and Access
contexts.purpose: Owns users, role assignments, sessions, privileged access grants and access reviews.

invariants.rule: Identities and permissions are tenant-scoped
Conflicting permissions cannot be held together
Privileged roles require MFA
Revocation takes effect immediately
Approved by someone other than the requester
Time-limited, with purpose recorded
Every item is confirmed or revoked before completion

contexts.name: Audit
contexts.purpose: Keeps an append-only record of every sensitive operation.
contexts.note: No aggregates. Audit events are append-only records, not a model with behaviour.

relationships.flows: Static data versions (all contexts consume these)
Processes, tasks and approvals (all contexts use this)
Tenant context (every context conforms to Tenancy)

processes.name: General quote to cash
processes.goal: From an accepted quote to an issued, billed, paid and accounted policy.

steps.step: AcceptQuote on an issued, valid quote
IssuePolicy from the accepted quote version

steps.compensation: Regenerate on failure; the policy is not rolled back

steps.step: AccrueCommission at the plan version in force

steps.compensation: If the payment fails or is reversed: PaymentReversed, the invoice reopens and arrears rules apply

steps.step: PostBusinessEvent for invoice, receipt, commission and cession
steps.compensation: On posting failure: PostingFailed goes to an exception queue; nothing is half-posted

processes.name: Life proposal to policy
processes.goal: From a captured application to an issued life policy.

steps.compensation: If ineligible, the proposal cannot be submitted
Decline or postpone ends the process; the proposal moves to Declined or Postponed

processes.name: General claim to settlement
processes.goal: From first notification of loss to payment, accounting and reinsurance recovery.

steps.step: AppointAssessor; the LossAssessment is reported and accepted

steps.compensation: On rejection, the claim stays under assessment
Instruction amount cannot exceed the approved amount

steps.step: Add to payout batch, approve and release

steps.compensation: On PaymentFailed: instruction returns to Failed, then is re-released with corrected details

processes.name: Health care to provider payment
processes.goal: From enrolment through preauthorisation and claim to provider payment.

steps.compensation: On rejection the provider is told; no reservation is made

steps.step: ValidateClaim, AdjudicateClaim: tariff, limits, co-payment, preauthorisation match

steps.compensation: On an optimistic-lock conflict, adjudication retries

steps.step: ApproveForPayment, then the ProviderPaymentRun is cut off, approved and released

steps.compensation: On ReverseClaim: ConsumeBenefit is reversed and a recovery is raised

processes.name: Product publication
processes.goal: From draft configuration to a product version that domains can sell.

steps.compensation: Validation errors keep the version in Draft

steps.step: Load the new rating version into cache

processes.name: Missed premium to lapse
processes.goal: From an unpaid instalment to lapse, with commission clawback.

steps.step: PaymentFailed or no payment by the due date

steps.compensation: A payment received in grace clears it (PaymentAllocated)

steps.step: LapsePolicy when grace ends and missed payments reach the limit
ReinstatePolicy within the reinstatement window, if requested and evidence accepted

glossary.meaning: A sellable insurance offering. In Product Factory it has many versions; in a domain, a policy refers to exactly one version.
An immutable, approved configuration of a product with an effective period. Transactions keep a reference to it.

Life: a contract on insured lives with benefits and beneficiaries. General: a contract on risk objects for a period of cover. Health uses Membership instead. Billing and Finance see only a policy reference.
A principal member's enrolment in a health plan option, with dependants. The health equivalent of a policy.
An application for cover submitted for underwriting.
A priced offer for cover, valid for a period. General quotes are versioned.
A person whose life or health is covered by a life policy.
Something insured under a general policy: a vehicle, building, vessel, cargo, equipment or liability.
An amount payable on a defined event. Life: death, disability, critical illness, maturity. Health: a category of care with limits.
Protection on a risk object against defined perils, with a sum insured, limits and excess.
The amount payable under a life benefit.
The maximum amount payable for a risk object or coverage.
The part of a loss the insured pays before the insurer pays.
The member's share of a health claim, as a percentage or amount.
A period after joining during which a benefit cannot be claimed.
A change to a general policy during its period, with any premium adjustment.
A change to a life policy, checked against its state, product rules and authority.
A life policy ending because premiums were not paid within the grace period. It may be reinstated within a window.
Approval of health care before it is given, with an authorised amount and validity period.
A recorded answer to whether a member can receive a service now.
Deciding a claim against cover, limits, rules and evidence. Each domain does its own.
The shared registration of a claim: number, evidence, communications and payments. It does not decide the claim.
An amount set aside for the expected cost of an open claim, changed only through financial movements.
Money recovered after a claim payment: from a third party, from salvage or from a reinsurer.
The share of a risk and its premium passed to a reinsurer under a treaty or facultative arrangement.
A periodic listing of ceded risks or claims sent to a reinsurer.
The payer relationship that invoices and collections are raised against.
Applying a received payment to invoices or instalments.
A balanced set of subledger entries for one business event. Posted journals are corrected only by reversal.
A broker, agent, bancassurer, aggregator or employer that distributes products under a permission.
A control where the person who prepares a sensitive change cannot be the one who approves it.
An insurer or insurance business operating on the platform. Every record belongs to exactly one tenant, except platform-global static data.
Reference, configuration and master data that governs transactions and changes through approved versions.
